sentence: A 74-year-old man with a history of ischemic heart disease was treated with beta-blockers, isosorbide mononitrate, antiplatelet agents, and proton pump inhibitors.

Referred to Digestive System consultation due to a 9-month history of intense asthenia, anorexia and progressive increase in sweating, with 15 kg weight loss, associated with diffuse abdominal pain and abdominal distension.
Analytically, iron deficiency anemia was observed.
Among other diagnostic tests, colonoscopy with sedation is requested.

A first colonoscopy was performed, showing from the rectum to the cecum an infinite number of sessile lesions with a polypoid appearance measuring between 3-6 mm, more frequent in number in the right colon and which form conglomerates at the level of the ileocecal valve, also affecting the terminal ileum.
The pathological anatomy of biopsies at different levels was nonspecific colitis with lymphoid follicular hyperplasia and eosinophilic infiltrate that reached 60% of inflammatory cells.
After the results obtained and given the patient's progressive clinical worsening, it was decided to perform gastroscopy and repeat colonoscopy to take new biopsies.

Multiple sessile polypoid lesions of different sizes (greater 8-9 mm) are observed in the gastric and duodenal mucosa, irregular, bulging with marked vascularization, some eroded at their apex, decreasing in number as one advances towards the distal duodenum, also confirming the lesions described. in the previous colonoscopy.

The histopathological result of the gastric, duodenal and colon biopsies was a dense diffuse lymphoid infiltrate in the mucosa and submucosa with glandular destruction and lymphoepithelial lesion, with small lymphocytes and a centrocytoid habit with positivity for CD 20, cyclin D1, and bcl-2. with a Ki-67 of 30%, all of which is compatible with gastric, small intestine and colon infiltration due to mantle lymphoma.

After the endoscopic findings, the patient is referred to the hematology service where studies are completed, which confirm the definitive diagnosis of stage IVB mantle non-Hodgkin lymphoma with gastric and small and large intestine involvement.
